vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: garden
Version: 1.1.3

The skill is classified as suspicious due to potential prompt injection vulnerabilities. While the `SKILL.md` explicitly states 'No external APIs called' and 'No telemetry or analytics', and the skill's primary function is local garden data management, several markdown files (`memory-template.md`, `tracking.md`, `climate-setup.md`, `diagnostics.md`) instruct the agent to log user-derived information into local markdown files. If this logged content contains malicious markdown (e.g., `[link](javascript:...)`), and the agent later interprets or renders these logs, it could lead to prompt injection against the agent. Additionally, `memory-template.md` instructs the agent to execute shell commands (`mkdir`, `touch`), which, while benign with hardcoded paths, demonstrates a capability that could be exploited if arguments were user-controlled.

llm.summary: The skill is an instruction-only local garden tracker that reads/writes files under ~/garden and asks for explicit user consent before touching any external workspace memory — its requirements and behavior are coherent with its stated purpose.

dimensions.detail: Name/description (garden tracking, planning, diagnostics) align with the instructions: creating and maintaining files under ~/garden, loading per-plant/zone files on demand, logging activities, and using manual climate config. No unrelated binaries, credentials, or network access are requested.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: All runtime guidance is local-file focused (~/garden/*) and stays within the garden domain. The only operation that reaches outside this directory is optional workspace integration: adding an entry to the user's main memory file (e.g., MEMORY.md) — the SKILL.md says this happens only with explicit consent. That outward write is reasonable for cross-session discovery but is somewhat vague about which file/path is modified and when consent is re-checked.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: Instruction-only skill with no install spec, no downloads, and no code files — lowest-risk install surface (nothing is written except the garden files the skill itself documents).
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: No environment variables, credentials, or external service tokens are requested. The only privileged action is optional addition to the user's main memory file (workspace integration), which the docs state requires explicit user approval.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: Skill persists data under ~/garden (explicit and expected). always:false. It can update a central memory file if the user consents; because the consent flow is emphasized, this is acceptable, but the exact target path for the main memory file is not strictly specified, so users should confirm where the entry will be written before approving.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill appears to do what it says: it will create and maintain files in ~/garden and otherwise operate locally. Before enabling workspace integration, confirm exactly which file(s) the skill will modify (the 'main memory' file and its path) and only grant that consent if you want other sessions/skills to see the Garden entry. If you prefer full local isolation, decline the integration prompt — the skill can still answer questions and log to ~/garden. As always, review the ~/garden files it creates and back them up if the data is important to you.
